page_title: Current Proof | Encrypted Sensitive Record Sync
title: Encrypted records, token lifecycle, and bounded background sync
summary: A narrow secure-systems runtime slice: encrypted provider tokens and authorized payloads, deterministic stub sync by default, opt-in sandbox HTTPS, and a live lab that shows grants, denied reads, and audited access.

challenge.title: Challenge
items: The proof needed visible evidence for encrypted-at-rest storage, token handling, and explicit integration boundaries instead of only architecture notes.
The implementation had to stay bounded and honest about scope, without implying real healthcare or production provider operations.
The public surface needed one stored-record path that could show guest-safe redaction, denied reads, and audited authorized access.

implementation.title: Implementation
items: Added one sensitive-data bounded context across domain, app, infra, and HTTP without breaking the repo into extra crates.
Stored provider tokens and authorized record payloads with AES-256-GCM, while keeping only redacted labels and last-four evidence queryable in cleartext.

Built a two-mode provider boundary: deterministic local stub by default, plus an opt-in sandbox HTTP adapter with credential exchange, bounded retry/backoff, cursor-based sync, key-versioned ciphertext storage, persisted grants, and a live lab panel for denied-versus-allowed reads.

outcomes.title: Outcomes
items: The repo now backs secure-systems claims with a running encrypted-storage and background-sync slice instead of only narrative direction.
Reviewers can inspect token status, last sync state, redacted records, ciphertext evidence, denied reads, and audited authorized access in the live app.
The proof stays sanitized and bounded: deterministic stub mode for repeatable review, opt-in sandbox mode for real outbound HTTPS, and explicit trust boundaries.

title: Automated fundraiser acknowledgments to remove high-volume backlog
summary: This archived GoodUnited case study covers replacing a manual thank-you workflow with browser automation that increased throughput and consistency under operational pressure.

challenge.title: Challenge
items: Manual thank-you workflows were time-consuming, error-prone, and perpetually behind demand.
Teams depended on queue dashboards and manual triage but still accumulated backlog.
Large nonprofit clients generated very high monthly fundraiser volume, making manual scaling expensive.

implementation.title: Implementation
items: Built a Playwright + TypeScript automation worker to emulate the existing browser workflow end to end.
Encoded template selection and variable substitution logic to reduce operator variance and mistakes.
Scaled execution to 72 concurrent instances to keep pace with continuously arriving fundraiser pages.

outcomes.title: Outcomes
items: Delivered roughly 12x speed compared to a single manual operator for the same task shape.
Eliminated persistent backlog and reduced error rates in outbound fundraiser communication.
Faster response windows increased fundraiser engagement and improved downstream support effectiveness.

title: Replaced delayed CSV workflows with realtime fundraiser + donation visibility
summary: This archived fundraiser pipeline moved operations from delayed CSV snapshots to realtime creation and donation signals integrated with Meta APIs.

challenge.title: Challenge
items: Prior workflow depended on manually downloaded CSV files that were at least 48 hours delayed.
Teams could only see fundraisers after donations appeared, missing newly created but not-yet-donated pages.
The lag degraded outreach speed and reduced the ability to guide fundraisers effectively.

implementation.title: Implementation
items: Built an Express + Svelte + MongoDB app for event participants to create fundraisers in one click.
Integrated Meta APIs so fundraiser creation events were captured at source instead of inferred later.
Surfaced donation activity in realtime, enabling chat and success teams to operate with current context.

outcomes.title: Outcomes
items: Eliminated 48-hour baseline delay in fundraiser discovery and donation context.
Enabled operations across millions of users and tens of millions of donation data points.
Improved decision quality across sales, customer success, and analytics functions.

title: Built a custom Substack publishing platform around a CMS event pipeline
summary: This archived Rust publishing platform ingests Directus CMS events, processes them through queued workers, and executes automated publishing flows through a custom Substack integration.

challenge.title: Challenge
items: Editorial and publishing workflows needed reliable automation across CMS content lifecycle events.
Substack operations required custom integration logic because official API support was limited for needed flows.
The system had to preserve determinism and observability across asynchronous event processing.

implementation.title: Implementation
items: Built a custom Substack client/integration layer for publish-oriented automation paths.
Typed Directus webhook events by collection/operation and routed them into queue-backed processing.
Structured a 13-crate Rust workspace across libs, services, and tools to keep boundaries explicit.
Used Axum services and worker processing to run end-to-end automation chains from trigger to publish.

outcomes.title: Outcomes
items: Replaced manual handoff-heavy publishing work with deterministic event-driven automation.
Created a reusable platform foundation for additional CMS-triggered automation chains.
Established a clear hardening roadmap through architecture review of reliability and CI/security gaps.
